name: San-Tash Burial Mound Complex
near: The settlement of San-Tash — about 0.9 km; the mound is 500 m from the Tup — Kegen road (A-363/A-364). Larger places: the village of Tup (~30 km to the west), Karakol (~56–79 km).
elev: 1,992–1,996 m above sea level (silkadv.com — 1,992 m; Nomad's Land — 1,996 m). The nearby San-Tash Pass is 2,166–2,195 m.
short: San-Tash (“counted stones”) is a huge stone heap over a Saka kurgan of the 6th–1st centuries BC near the San-Tash Pass on the way to Kazakhstan, tied to a legend about Tamerlane’s army.
desc: The San-Tash burial mound complex lies in the Tup river valley between the Kungey and Terskey Ala-Too ranges, 500 m from the Tup — Kegen road. The central mound is a stone heap 4 m high and 50–56 m in diameter (more than 3,500 m³ of stone) with a crater left by an ancient robbers’ shaft; around it are more than 250 large and small kurgans of the Saka period (6th–1st centuries BC), burials of nomad chiefs, as well as the ruins of a caravanserai of the 10th–12th centuries (a 48 m square with a tower). According to legend, Timur (Tamerlane) ordered each warrior to lay a stone before the campaign to China and take one back on the return; the stones that were left showed the number of the dead — hence the name. No modern excavations have been carried out. The famous east wind “santash” blows from the pass, raising storms on Issyk-Kul.
guide: Stop at the Tup — Kegen road: it is 500 m on foot across a meadow to the mound. Climb the four-metre pile of stones — you can see the crater in the centre, a trace of ancient robbers; from there make out dozens of smaller mounds around — that is the Saka necropolis, two and a half thousand years old. Locals will tell you the legend of Tamerlane, but remember: the kurgans are a thousand years older than his campaign. If you are continuing to Karkyra or to Kazakhstan via Kegen, it is an ideal “warm-up” stop; there is no ticket office or cafe nearby, but there is always wind — not for nothing is the wind that whips up storms on Issyk-Kul called “santash”. In spring and September the Tup valley is golden, and in summer it is cooler here than on the lakeshore.
see: The central stone mound (4 m, Ø 50–56 m) with its crater; a field of 250+ small kurgans; the ruins of the 10th–12th century caravanserai; a panorama of the Tup valley and Kungey Ala-Too; on the way — the San-Tash Pass (2,166–2,195 m) with spruce slopes and the Jergalan valley.
skip: You want “impressive” ruins — outwardly it is a heap of stones in a field, and the value lies in history and context. You are not heading towards Tup/Karkyra/Kegen — driving 60–80 km from Karakol specially for a 20-minute stop is not for everyone. Strong wind and rain — it is uncomfortable on the open mound.
diff: Very easy: 500 m across a flat meadow from the road and a climb onto a 4 m mound.
when: May — October; in summer (July–August) combine it with the nomad games at Karkyra. In winter the San-Tash Pass can be hard to cross because of snow (silkadv).
hours: An open area with no fence or ticket office, around the clock.
daytime: Morning or the hour before sunset — low sun emphasises the relief of the mounds and the crater; during the day the open field is windy.
how: From Karakol east through Tup along the Kegen road (A-363/A-364), ~79 km via Tup or ~56 km via Novoznesenovka and the Kok-Kiya farm, then over the San-Tash Pass; the mound is 500 m to the right of the road, 0.9 km from the settlement of San-Tash. From the Kazakhstan side — 10–15 km from the Karkyra — Kegen border crossing.
needcar: Yes: public transport to the settlement of San-Tash is limited (marshrutkas (minibuses) Karakol — Tup, then a taxi/hitchhike); it is easier by car or with a tour to Karkyra/Kazakhstan.
self: Yes: no permits or fees; the mound is visible from the road. The border zone starts closer to the border crossing; documents are not checked at the mound, but keep your passport with you (it is a border area).
roadtype: From Karakol to Tup — paved; the section over the San-Tash Pass (A-364) is a broken gravel-and-rock road with potholes (silkadv), passable for a passenger car in the dry season; the last 500 m on foot across the meadow.
traveltime: Karakol — San-Tash ~1–1.5 h (56–79 km depending on the route); from the Karkyra border crossing ~15–20 min; the visit takes 20–40 min.
stay: There is no accommodation at the mound. Nearest: guesthouses and yurts in the Karkyra valley (in summer, via CBT/Destination Karakol), guesthouses in Tup; the main choice is Karakol (60–80 km). 2025–2026 prices not confirmed.
net: Along the Tup — Kegen road there is mobile coverage near the settlements (the settlement of San-Tash is 0.9 km away); on the pass and in the Karkyra valley the signal is unstable. No reports on specific operators were found.
entry: Free: no ticket offices, fences or fees (silkadv, Nomad's Land, Atlas Obscura — no fee is mentioned).
transfer: No offers with a price specifically to San-Tash were found; a guide — a taxi from Karakol to the Tup district by agreement, tours to Karkyra via Destination Karakol/CBT (on request).
bring: A windbreaker (constant “santash” wind), a hat, water and a snack (no cafe nearby), a passport (border area), a wide-angle camera for the valley panorama.
warn: Border zone with Kazakhstan: do not walk from the mounds towards the border without documents; a passport is needed at the border crossing. Do not dismantle or move stones — it is an archaeological monument. On the San-Tash Pass the road is broken, with snowdrifts in winter; wind tears tents and raises storms on the lake. The Tamerlane legend is folklore: the monument is Saka, a thousand years older.
food: In Tup and at Karkyra in summer — kumys, boorsok, kuurdak from herders; the nearest cafes are in Tup and Karakol. There is no food at the mound.
reviews: 2GIS: 5/5, 6 ratings, 2 reviews (07.10.2026). Google Maps: no separate listing matched (meta: ambiguous result). TripAdvisor: listing not found. From descriptions: pros — atmosphere, the legend, the view of the valley; cons — “just a pile of stones”, far from Karakol.
p.sum: San-Tash is a 20–40-minute stop by the Tup — Kegen road (A-363/A-364): the central stone mound 500 m to the right of the highway, 0.9 km from the settlement of San-Tash. It is worth coming here specially only on the way to Karkyra or to Kazakhstan via the Karkyra — Kegen border crossing (open 24 hours since 11.2024). From Karakol — 1–1.5 h by car or taxi; the Karakol — Almaty bus (since 7.09.2025, 1,200 som) passes by, but you need to arrange a drop-off. The nearest comfortable overnight is the Ak-Sai yurt camp at Karkyra (from $45 for a tent for two with breakfast, horse $15/h) or Karakol.

p.season: May–June: green Tup valley, cool, windy. July–August: the best time, herders and yurts at Karkyra, nomad games. September–October: golden valley, few people. November–April: the San-Tash Pass gets snowed in, frost, wind; in winter at Karkyra — Ak-Sai glamping with snowmobiles.
p.budget.economy: ≈1,500–2,500 som per person: marshrutka to Tup + taxi/hitchhike, free entry, food 500–800; overnight in Karakol in a hostel $10–25.
p.budget.comfort: ≈8,000–12,000 som per person: a car with a driver for the day (≈5,000 som per group), a night at Karkyra Yurt Camp $65–95 for two with meals, horse ride $15/h.
p.permits: Not required: no ticket offices or fees. It is a border area — keep your passport with you; for crossing the border — the Karkyra — Kegen crossing (24 hours since 11.2024).
p.access: With children and older people — yes (500 m across a flat meadow). With a stroller — partly, over grass. With a dog — yes. Strong wind — bring a windbreaker.
